transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I go out of my way to avoid anything that reminds me of what happened to my cousin, even if it means cutting out parts of my life. He was killed during an armed robbery in Guatemala a little over a year ago, and I've been pulling back from so many things since then. It's gotten to the point where it is really affecting my day-to-day life and my relationships.
Do you also experience upsetting, unwanted memories, nightmares, or sudden flashbacks about what happened to your cousin?

Yes, all the time. Out of nowhere, like when I'm at my desk or cooking, I'll suddenly see my cousin in his coffin or hear my aunt describing the shooting, which makes my chest tighten and I just freeze. I also have these vivid, awful nightmares about buses and my family back home that wake me up joltingly, leaving me completely exhausted.
Have you also found yourself feeling constantly on edge, easily startled, or unusually watchful of your surroundings since this happened?

Yes, I feel constantly on edge. If someone walks up behind me at work or a car backfires on the street, I jump out of my skin and my heart just races. Even after I realize it's nothing, it takes me a really long time to calm back down.
Have you also noticed changes in your mood or how you think since this happened, such as feeling detached from loved ones or losing interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Yes, absolutely. I used to live for salsa dancing and hiking, but now I feel completely flat and disconnected, and I've lost interest in doing them at all. I also feel so detached from my family—even when my daughter gets an award, I just go through the motions of smiling but feel totally muted and unable to feel close to anyone inside.
Have these symptoms—the nightmares, avoidance, and feeling constantly on edge—been happening regularly for more than a month?
Yes, they have been going on for much longer than a month. These feelings started pretty steadily right after I came back to New York from my cousin's funeral, so it's been a little over a year now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.1) following the traumatic loss of their cousin in an armed robbery. They report persistent intrusion symptoms (nightmares, flashbacks, intrusive memories), avoidance of trauma-related reminders, negative alterations in cognition and mood (emotional numbing, detachment, loss of interest in activities), and marked alterations in arousal and reactivity (exaggerated startle response, hypervigilance). These symptoms have persisted for over a year and cause significant functional impairment in daily life and relationships.
